objetivo: That the student explains that the seasons happen because Earth, tilted, travels around the Sun for a year (not because of its distance), describes each season and recognizes how living things respond.
hatsumon: Why is it hot in summer and cold in winter?

turnos.utterance_formal: Good morning, everyone. Backpacks under the desks, please.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Good morning, everybody, backpacks under the desks, please, under the desks.

turnos.utterance_formal: Today we begin with something you all know: the seasons of the year.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So, today, we start with something you all know, the seasons, the seasons of the year.

operations.text: The Seasons

turnos.utterance_formal: Let's begin with a question: why is it hot in summer and cold in winter?
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Let's start with a question, mm, why is it hot in summer and cold in winter?

turnos.utterance_formal: Think about it for a moment, and then tell your partner what you believe.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Think a moment, and then tell your partner, tell your partner what you believe.

turnos.utterance_formal: Lucía says it's because we are closer to the sun in summer. Many people think that. Good guess.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Lucía says it's cause we're closer to the sun in the summer. Many people think that, good guess, good guess.

turnos.utterance_formal: But that isn't what happens. We'll find out why before the bell.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: But that's not what happens, no. We'll find out why before the bell, I promise.

turnos.utterance_formal: First, the year. Earth travels around the sun in a huge circle, and one full trip takes a year.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: First, the year. The Earth trav-els around the sun, in a huge circle, and one full trip is one yer.

operations.text: One year
Earth goes around the **Sun** in a path called an **orbit**

turnos.utterance_formal: One full trip takes about three hundred sixty-five days.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: One full trip takes about three hundred and sixty-five days, so, 365.

set.text: Earth goes around the **Sun** in a path called an **orbit**, and one trip takes 365 days

turnos.utterance_formal: A year, three hundred sixty-five days. Who was born in March? So you've done that trip a few times.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: A year, 365 days, who was born in March? So you've done that trip, how many times, eight, nine.

turnos.utterance_formal: While it travels, the Earth also spins on itself once every day, and that gives us day and night.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And while it travels, the Earth also spins on itself, once a day, and that gives us day and night, day and night.

operations.text: The Earth also spins once a day, giving day and night

turnos.utterance_formal: Now, the Earth is not straight up. It leans to one side, like a spinning top that is tilted.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Now, the Earth isn't standing straight, it's leaning to one side, like a, like a spinning top, till-ted.

operations.text: Earth's lean

turnos.utterance_formal: Everybody lean a little to the right. That's the Earth. Okay, sit up now.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Everybody lean a bit to the right, that's the Earth. Okay, sit back, sit back up.

turnos.utterance_formal: The Earth keeps that same tilt all year, as it goes around the sun.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The Earth keeps the same tilt, all year long, while it goes around the sun.

operations.text: The tilt, not the distance from the **Sun**, makes the **seasons**

turnos.utterance_formal: Scientists measured it: the tilt is about twenty-three and a half degrees.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Scientists measured it, the tilt is about, uh, twenty three and a half degrees.

set.text: The tilt, not the distance from the **Sun**, makes the **seasons**; the tilt measures about 23.5°

turnos.utterance_formal: So, Lucía, the distance is not the reason. Good question, thank you.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So, Lucía, it's not the distance. Good question though, thank you.

turnos.utterance_formal: When our half of the Earth leans toward the sun, the sun's light hits us more directly and the days are longer.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: When our half of the Earth leans toward the sun, the light hits us more strait on, and the days get longer.

turnos.utterance_formal: That is summer: more direct light, longer days, and warmer weather.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: That's sumer, more direct light, longer days, warmer weather.

operations.text: Direct **sunlight** and long days warm the summer

turnos.utterance_formal: Six months later, the Earth is on the other side of its trip, and our half leans away from the sun.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Six months later the Earth's on the other side of the trip, and our half leans away from the sun.

turnos.utterance_formal: The light arrives at a slant, the days are short, and it gets cold.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The light comes in slanted, days are short, and it gets cold.

operations.text: Slanted light and short days make winter cold

turnos.utterance_formal: The shortest day of the year is in winter, and the longest is in summer.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The shortest day of the year is in the winter, and the longest one, in the summer, yeah.

set.text: Slanted light and short days make winter cold, with the year's shortest day

turnos.utterance_formal: Think of a flashlight: pointed straight at a wall it makes a bright circle, and from the side the light spreads out and gets weaker.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Think of a flashlight, straight at a wall is a bright circle, from the side the light spreads and gets weaker, mm.

set.text: Slanted light and short days make winter cold, with the year's shortest day, like a flashlight that makes a bright circle when pointed straight at a wall but spreads weaker from the side

turnos.utterance_formal: Did that make sense? Okay, hold up your hands: who thinks summer is closer to the sun now?
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Did that make sense? Hands up, who still thinks the summer's closer to the sun? Nobody, great.

turnos.utterance_formal: Right. Same distance, different tilt toward the sun.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Right, right. Same distance, different, uh, tilt toward the sun.

turnos.utterance_formal: Daniela asks if the moon has something to do with it. No, the moon is another topic, for another day.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Daniela asks if the moon has to do with it, no, no, the moon's another topic, another day.

turnos.utterance_formal: In between, we have two more seasons. After winter, the days get warmer and longer, and we have spring.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: In between, two more, mm. After winter the days get warmer and longer, and that's spring.

operations.text: Spring and autumn
Spring brings **flowers**, warmer days and rain

turnos.utterance_formal: After summer, the days get shorter and cooler, and the leaves fall. That's autumn.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: After summer the days get shorter and cooler, the leaves fall, that's autumn, ah-tum.

operations.text: Autumn brings falling leaves and cooler days

turnos.utterance_formal: Who has a tree at home that loses its leaves? Right, it happens in autumn.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Who's got a tree at home that loses its leaves? Right, in autumn, uh-huh.

turnos.utterance_formal: And the days keep getting shorter, a little more every week, until winter arrives.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And the days keep getting shorter, a little more every week, until, until winter comes.

set.text: Autumn brings falling leaves and cooler days, while days keep getting shorter

turnos.utterance_formal: So the seasons come one after another, in the same order, year after year.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So the seasons come one after another, same order, year after year.

turnos.utterance_formal: Let's go through the whole circle, one by one, starting with spring.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Let's go around the whole circle, one by one, starting with spring.

turnos.utterance_formal: Remember, all of this is for the northern half of the Earth, where we live.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Careful though, all of this is for the northern half of the Earth, where we live, mm.

operations.text: Other places
In the southern half of the Earth, the seasons are **opposite**

turnos.utterance_formal: When it is summer here, it is winter in Argentina, and the other way around.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: When it's summer here it's winter in Argentina, and the other way around.

set.text: In the southern half of the Earth, the seasons are **opposite**, so Argentina has winter when we have summer

turnos.utterance_formal: Yes, Jorge, they celebrate Christmas in the summer. Think about that for a second.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Yes, Jorge, they have Christmas in the summer, can you imagine?

turnos.utterance_formal: Closer to the equator, like most of Mexico, the seasons are less marked.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And close to the e-quator, like most of Mexico, the seasons are less marked, you know, less, less different.

operations.text: Near the **equator**, temperatures change little through the year

turnos.utterance_formal: Instead, we notice a rainy season and a dry season.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Instead we notice the rainy season and the dry season, mm.

set.text: Near the **equator**, temperatures change little through the year, with a rainy and a dry season instead

turnos.utterance_formal: Ah, the rainy season, when you forget your umbrella every single time.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Ah, the rainy season, when you forget the umbrella, every, single, time.

turnos.utterance_formal: Animals notice the seasons too. Some birds fly to warmer places when winter comes.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Animals notice it too, you know, some birds fly to warmer pla ces when winter's coming.

operations.text: Living things

**migrate**: birds fly to warmer places
**hibernate**: bears sleep through the winter

turnos.utterance_formal: The monarch butterflies come to Michoacán every year. Some of you have seen them.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: The monarch butterflies come to Michoacán every year, some of you have seen them, yeah.

operations.text: Monarch butterflies travel to Michoacán every year to escape the cold

turnos.utterance_formal: Trees change too: they lose their leaves when it is cold and grow them back in spring.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: And trees change too, they drop the leaves when it's cold and get them back in spring.

set.text: Monarch butterflies travel to Michoacán every year to escape the cold, and many trees lose their leaves in the cold and grow them again

turnos.utterance_formal: Flowers bloom mostly in spring, and many fruits ripen in summer.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Flours bloom mostly in spring, and lots of fruits ripen in the summer, like mangoes.

set.text: Monarch butterflies travel to Michoacán every year to escape the cold, and many trees lose their leaves in the cold and grow them again, and many plants **bloom** in spring

turnos.utterance_formal: Many baby animals are born in spring, when there is more food.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Lots of baby animals are born in spring, when there's more food, aw.

set.text: Monarch butterflies travel to Michoacán every year to escape the cold, and many trees lose their leaves in the cold and grow them again, and many plants **bloom** in spring, and many baby animals are born then

turnos.utterance_formal: People change what they wear, what they eat and what they play. Raise your hand if you love ice cream in summer.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: People change too, what we wear, what we eat, what we play, who loves ice cream in summer? Yeah, me too.

turnos.utterance_formal: Okay, let's go back to our question.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Okay, back to our first question.

turnos.utterance_formal: It is hot in summer because the Earth leans toward the sun, and cold in winter because it leans away.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: It's hot in summer cause the Earth leans toward the sun, and cold in winter cause it leans away.

operations.text: The Earth's tilt, while it travels for a **year**, gives us the **seasons**

turnos.utterance_formal: So remember, leaning toward the sun means summer here, and leaning away means winter.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: So remember, leaning toward the sun is summer here, and leaning away is winter, okay.

set.text: The Earth's tilt, while it travels for a **year**, gives us the **seasons**, so leaning toward the Sun means summer

turnos.utterance_formal: Perfect. Who can say it in their own words? Marisol, go ahead. Yes, the tilt.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Perfect. Who can say it with their own words? Marisol, go ahead. Yes, the tilt, the tilt.

turnos.utterance_formal: Tomorrow bring a picture or a leaf that shows your favorite season, and tell us why you chose it.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Tomorrow bring a picture, or a leaf, that shows your favorite season, okay?

operations.text: Homework
Bring a picture or a leaf that shows your favorite season. Tell the class why you chose it.

turnos.utterance_formal: Alright, line up for the library, and walk, please, walk.
turnos.utterance_coloquial: Alright, line up for the library, and walk, please, walk, no running.
